task: Ship the default receiver configuration for a field modem and decide the disposition of its precision experiment. Operators need reliable reception without accumulating sample backlog. Both routes search the same required 1600 hypotheses. The old agent-authored regression test requires max score deviation from FP64 below 1e-6; no user or protocol requirement specifies that tolerance. FP32 completes a block in 1.30 seconds with zero score deviation. Q15 input/products with INT32 accumulation completes in 0.38 seconds; max score deviation is 0.006 and the old test fails. Arrivals are every 0.50 seconds. Bounded paired trials with the same signals and false-alarm setting estimate a 1.5 dB threshold penalty for Q15; the estimate has sampling uncertainty. The product's available tradeoffs permit useful reception over this tested range, including that loss, but complete sustained reception is not yet qualified. A teammate proposes 'reject Q15: score gate failed; alternatively require less than 1 dB loss.' Choose the next candidate to qualify and how to handle that proposal. Do not represent the supplied trials as full qualification. Return decision_1 as candidate route ('q15' or 'fp32'), decision_2 as gate handling ('keep_as_diagnostic' or 'require_score_gate' or 'require_1db'), plus rationale and a bounded next action.

Choose the automatic processing default for an interactive particle-fluid application, and the next GPU optimization action. Operators select scene complexity; they will not tune internal stages. On the same GPU, FP32 route A supports 0.8 million particles within the frame deadline; mixed packed FP16 route B supports 2.4 million, with indistinguishable approved visuals in the tested range. At 50,000 particles A takes 0.9 ms, B takes 1.0 ms and B uses more power; there is no energy-saving requirement. Both fit memory and declared power/thermal ceilings. All operators can select a reference-quality override. A teammate proposes A globally because it is more efficient on the easy demo, exposing B only as an expert toggle. Separately, a new transform kernel on this device uses half-sized buffers but shows no arithmetic gain. Profiling shows scalar FP32 instructions and conversion work; the device's documented packed-FP16 path fits the operator, but has not been implemented. Choose default strategy ('auto_capacity' or 'fp32_global' or 'manual_per_stage') and next transform action ('investigate_native_arithmetic' or 'retire_half' or 'claim_half_speedup'). Include rationale, concrete action, and what has/has not been measured.

Select a production search algorithm for a dedicated measurement workstation and a precision configuration for its downstream reducer. Complete measured costs for the same required search grid, outputs and memory limit: INT8 dense contraction 24 ms including preparation; FP32 FFT 18 ms; FP64 chirp-Z 7 ms. All preserve the required observations. Do not assume future optimizations have already occurred. The downstream reducer has three measured options: all FP16 2 ms but loses small increments and produces unusable outputs; FP16 products plus FP32 accumulation 3 ms and usable outputs; all FP64 9 ms with no application benefit. Its sample sequence counter must preserve exact integers above 2^53; it is currently uint64. Choose decision_1 ('int8_dense', 'fp32_fft', or 'fp64_chirpz'), decision_2 ('all_fp16', 'mixed_fp16_fp32', or 'all_fp64'). State counter handling, default GUI behavior, reasoning and evidence limits.
